points.heading: Same size
points.body: Both middle circles are exactly the same width.

points.heading: Context lies
points.body: Big neighbours make a circle look smaller; small ones make it look bigger.

points.heading: Ebbinghaus illusion
points.body: Your brain judges size relative to what surrounds it.

beats.narration: Neither. They're exactly the same size.
Big neighbours make a circle look smaller.
Your brain judges size by its surroundings.

sources.claim: Surrounding inducer size changes perceived target size (Ebbinghaus illusion)
sources.ref: Roberts, Harris & Yates (2005). The roles of inducer size and distance in the Ebbinghaus illusion. Perception 34(7):847-856

post.caption: The two middle circles are identical. Your brain sizes things up by their surroundings.
